quick: Insufficient data; use only if needed
Reduce: 50 mg if moderate, 25 mg if severe/ESRD
Limit; hypoglycemia risk with other agents
summary: Sitagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor that improves glycemic control in type 2 diabetes by enhancing incretin hormones. Standard dose is 100 mg once daily, reduced to 50 mg or 25 mg in renal impairment. Generally weight-neutral with low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk; watch for pancreatitis and hypersensitivity.
indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
May be used as monotherapy or in combination with other antidiabetic agents (e.g., metformin, sulfonylurea, insulin)
admin: Take orally once daily, with or without food
Assess renal function before initiation and periodically
When combined with sulfonylurea or insulin, consider lowering those agents to reduce hypoglycemia
moa: Selectively inhibits dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4), the enzyme that degrades the incretin hormones GLP-1 and GIP. By prolonging active incretin levels, it increases glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppresses glucagon release, lowering fasting and postprandial glucose with low risk of hypoglycemia when used alone.

absolute: History of serious hypersensitivity to sitagliptin (anaphylaxis, angioedema, Stevens-Johnson syndrome)

preg: Available data are insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk for major birth defects or miscarriage. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed; many guidelines prefer insulin for diabetes in pregnancy.
lact: Insufficient data on presence in human milk; use with caution and weigh benefits against potential risk to the infant.
renal: Dose adjustment required: 50 mg once daily for eGFR 30 to <45 mL/min/1.73 m2, and 25 mg once daily for eGFR <30 including ESRD on dialysis. Assess renal function periodically.
hepatic: No dose adjustment in mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Not studied in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Sulfonylureas - increased risk of hypoglycemia; consider lowering sulfonylurea dose
moderate: Digoxin - slight increase in digoxin levels; monitor
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; increased hypoglycemia risk when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas.
interactions.diagnostics: May affect glucose and HbA1c readings (therapeutic intent).

rare: Hypersensitivity reactions (anaphylaxis, angioedema, exfoliative skin conditions)

monitoring: HbA1c every 3 months until target, then periodically
Renal function at baseline and periodically for dose adjustment
Signs and symptoms of pancreatitis (severe persistent abdominal pain)
Blood glucose, especially when combined with sulfonylurea or insulin
counsel: Take once daily, with or without food
Stop the drug and seek care for severe, persistent abdominal pain (pancreatitis)
Report severe joint pain or blistering skin reactions
Recognize and treat hypoglycemia if also taking sulfonylurea or insulin
Continue diet, exercise and other diabetes care
pk: Glucose-lowering within hours; full effect over weeks
pearls: Weight-neutral with low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk as monotherapy
Primarily renally cleared - dose-reduce in renal impairment
Can be combined with metformin, sulfonylureas, or insulin
Consider lowering sulfonylurea/insulin when adding to reduce hypoglycemia
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the regular once-daily schedule; do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Generally well tolerated; supportive care is the mainstay. Remove unabsorbed drug from the GI tract and monitor with ECG and clinical observation. Sitagliptin is modestly dialyzable; hemodialysis may be considered for severe overdose in renal impairment.
